question: What stops a proof that SCANS a corpus for a conforming case from passing BECAUSE OF the defect it should have caught? A tooth that searches for the first artifact matching the canonical shape skips every malformed one — so the more broken the corpus, the more certainly the tooth goes green.
whats_beyond: The instance is closed and the pattern is not. cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_transitions.py::test_it_parses_a_real_live_ticket_workflow_string scans CairnCommons/tickets/ for a ticket whose path already equals canonical; when state-machine-physics.json parsed to 9 states instead of 6, the scan silently moved on to a healthy ticket and passed. It was closed by a COMPANION tooth (test_prose_after_the_last_state_cannot_feed_phantom_states_onto_the_path) asserting EXACTLY on a constructed trap string — and that companion is a discipline someone remembered, not physics (Law 4). The generalisation: the same animal cleared as troubles/a-stale-fixture-masked-three-reds-in-intents-own-house.json, and the same shape as memory's leak-scan-coin-toss-red (a check that goes green for the wrong reason). Candidate answers to weigh: (a) a scanning tooth must also assert a DENOMINATOR — how many candidates it rejected, so a corpus of one healthy artifact reads differently from a corpus of ninety-six; (b) a scanning tooth is always paired with a constructed-trap tooth, enforced by the tester rather than by the author's memory; (c) the tester refuses a tooth whose assertion is reached only inside a search loop. Not settled here — this is the frontier, not a plan.

Re-read 2026-08-10 at the trouble's clear: candidate ONE (writer or door?) was answered by physics — skills/sorted/door.py:101 runs parse_workflow and parse_workflow refuses an unbracketed cursor, so /sorted cannot write an unreadable one. Candidate TWO is a design detail about how proofs are written, which the question corpus resolves, not Akien — so it is lifted here rather than held hostage inside a trouble whose own lived symptom is measurably gone (96 of 96 live tickets parse, measured 2026-08-10).

resolved.answer: Two answers, and neither alone is enough. (a) A scanning tooth asserts its DENOMINATOR — the count scanned, the count rejected, the position of the match — so a reader sees how selective the scan was. A corpus of one healthy artifact out of ninety-six reads differently from ninety-six out of ninety-six. This is measurement (Law 3). (b) For a specific defect, a constructed-trap companion is the physics (Law 4): it builds the exact failure shape and asserts the exact value, so the defect cannot be skipped. The companion pattern is already in place for the founding instance (test_prose_after_the_last_state_cannot_feed_phantom_states_onto_the_path). The denominator was missing; it is now added. (c) TESTER ENFORCEMENT of the pairing is an IOU: nothing yet prevents a scanning tooth from shipping without a companion. The companion is 'a discipline someone remembered, not physics' — as the question's own text says.
resolved.what_changed: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_transitions.py::test_it_parses_a_real_live_ticket_workflow_string — the scanning tooth now counts scanned/rejected and prints the denominator. Proof GREEN.
resolved.what_remains: Tester enforcement (candidate c) is the physics goal. A scan-pattern detector in the tester — or a mandatory companion declaration — would close the IOU. Until then, the denominator makes the selectivity visible and the companion convention is CC's discipline to follow.
